I don’t have a large, well-attested body of information on **Ascanio Albertini**. The name appears to refer to a relatively obscure early-modern Italian figure, most likely a **16th-century Catholic prelate** connected with the Kingdom of Naples.

What I can say with reasonable caution:

- **Ascanio Albertini** was an Italian ecclesiastical figure, apparently active in the **mid-to-late 1500s**.
- He is most commonly associated with the diocese of **Avellino e Frigento** — a historical bishopric in southern Italy, in what was then the Kingdom of Naples.
- He seems to have held the office of **Bishop of Avellino and Frigento** sometime during the 16th century.
- His episcopate would have fallen during or shortly after the period of the **Council of Trent** — 1545–1563 — when Catholic dioceses across Italy were being reshaped by Tridentine reform.
- He does not appear to be a widely known theologian, saint, writer, cardinal, or major political figure; surviving references to him are likely to be found in episcopal lists, diocesan histories, or Catholic-hierarchy catalogues rather than in broader historical narratives.

I do **not** have reliable details on:

- his birth date,
- his death date,
- his family background,
- his education,
- the exact dates of appointment and consecration,
- major writings or reforms,
- or specific events from his episcopate.

Because the name is obscure, there is also a possibility of confusion with another member of the Albertini family or another cleric of similar name. If you have a source, context, time period, or location where you encountered “Ascanio Albertini,” I can help identify him more precisely.
